rv.q: Lindsay nails the self-serving ruthlessness of Onassis as slightly out of character; he's happiest on home territory, moving to music, flapping a napkin.
But too often, the wordy text plays like a radio documentary drama, interspersed by Greek musical interludes and greatly amplified gunshots to mark the two Kennedy killings.
This isn’t theatre, it’s a dramatised gossip column.
This is a ridiculous play that treats a delusional tycoon as if a figure of epic grandeur.
His performance is a strong, forceful portrayal of one of the world's most devious men and he has cleverly caught much of the Onassis character and charisma.

cn.t: Lindsay's bravura performance as the shipping magnate stands out in Sherman's plodding biodrama that critics find laughably awful to moderately diverting, with most dismissing it as higher tosh despite slick production values.
